endpoints.intro: A protected buyer run may only reach a destination named here. An empty list is the intended default, not a failure: nothing has been approved yet, so every protected run is refused before it can spend anything.
endpoints.providerHint: The slug the adapter router actually serves (openai, anthropic, together, …)
endpoints.baseUrlHint: Stored normalized: https only, no embedded credentials, query string or fragment
endpoints.protectionHint: Required, no default: an admin states the protection class for this destination
endpoints.disclosureHint: What this provider records or retains about protected-run inputs, as reviewed. This is the posture the buyer is told before the run
endpoints.disclosurePlaceholder: e.g. Provider retains request and response logs for the credential owner for 30 days; no training on inputs.
endpoints.needBothDisclosures: A logging disclosure and a protection class are both required — a destination without them is not an approval.
endpoints.loadFailed: Could not load the approved endpoints
endpoints.emptyWhy: Until a row exists here, protected execution stops before the egress gate. That is the product's promise, not a bug.
endpoints.urlUnusable: This row can never match a run: {{error}}
endpoints.adapterMismatch: Adapter mismatch — a protected run on this provider builds {{expected}}, so this row is invisible to the gate

catalog.intro: The admin-reviewed catalog: which model identities exist, who developed them, and what has been reviewed as a release. Vendor (the developer) is the field an evidence-panel refusal asks an admin to record.
catalog.recordTitle: Record or refresh a reviewed entry
catalog.modelIdHint: Exact id. (provider, modelId) is unique, so re-recording refreshes that entry instead of duplicating it — and a field you leave blank is cleared. Use the vendor column below for a narrow correction.
catalog.vendorHint: Who developed the model, not who served it. Unknown never fills an evidence-panel slot
catalog.successorHint: Must already be in the catalog, under the same provider — lineage is reviewed, never guessed from a name
catalog.searchPlaceholder: Search model, provider, vendor or family
catalog.empty: No catalogued model matches this view
catalog.emptyWhy: The catalog is empty until a reviewer records an entry. Nothing here is inferred from user provider caches or name substrings.
catalog.eventsNote: A release event is what a reviewer recorded, with its own key so replaying the review notifies nobody twice. Suggestions only — they never start paid work.

evidence.intro: Every evidence publication the platform holds, with the manifest it was published under. Read-only: a withdrawal is the author's action, never an operator's.
evidence.empty: No evidence publication matches this view
evidence.manifestUnparsable: The stored manifest cannot be shown as a validated document: {{error}}
evidence.withdrawIsTheirs: The manifest is the public disclosure document itself. Nothing on this screen changes it, supersedes it or withdraws it.

spend.intro: Provider spend as the ledger records it: one row per logical operation. An operation with no price is NOT zero cost — a partially-priced set is shown as a floor plus the count still unpriced.
spend.loadFailed: Could not load the spend ledger
spend.noAttempts: No provider operation has been recorded against any account yet.
spend.readOnlyNote: Spend and approvals are append-only records of what was authorized and what happened. Nothing here refunds, revokes or edits a frozen plan, and no recorded figure is ever restated.

reprice.hint: A ledger row is priced once, as it is written. If the provider's price list was unreachable in that moment the row has read "cost unknown" ever since, even though the token counts it needs are stored beside it. This looks up those rows again at today's rates and fills only the ones with no figure.
reprice.stillUnknown: {{n}} still unknown — no price list names that model
reprice.aggregates: {{n}} run-level rows stay unknown: the ledger cannot name a single model or credential for them
reprice.remaining: {{n}} candidates were left past this pass — run it again
reprice.asOf: A re-priced row records today as the moment its rate was read, not the day the call ran.
